Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has been charged with six counts of corruption and power abuse involving RM427.5 million.  

Muhyiddin, who is the co-founder of Bersatu, pleaded not guilty and claimed trial to all six counts after the charges were read to him before Sessions Court judge Azura Alwi. 

Muhyiddin was charged with two counts of receiving RM195 million funds, that are proceeds from unlawful activities last year. The funds were credited into the party's CIMB bank account. 

He was also charged with four counts of using his position as the Prime Minister and Bersatu president to ask for RM200 million as a bribe from Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd. 

The Bersatu president, whose actual registered name is Mahiaddin Md Yasin, has become the second former prime minister to be charged in court for corruption in the country's history.

The political bromance that once defined Malaysian opposition politics has spectacularly combusted. Muhyiddin Yassin and Hamzah Zainuddin, formerly inseparable allies in their quest for Malay-Islamic political dominance, are now locked in open warfare after Hamzah's sudden dismissal from party leadership. What makes this split particularly fascinating is the competing narratives: Hamzah claims he has no idea why he was sacked and won't appeal the decision, while Muhyiddin insists he endured years of sabotage attempts and had to act to save the party. At least one of them is lying, and the spectacle of watching these self-proclaimed defenders of race and religion tear each other apart reveals something profound about the nature of Malaysian ethno-nationalist politics.

The irony is almost too perfect to ignore. These are the same leaders who constantly invoke Malay unity, who warn about the dangers of division, and who build entire political careers on the promise of a united ummah standing strong against perceived threats. Yet when given actual power and responsibility, they cannot even maintain unity within their own leadership circle. While their supporters are told to sacrifice for the cause, to donate money for legal battles, and to believe in the grand narrative of racial solidarity, the architects of this vision are busy destroying it from within. The pattern is depressingly familiar: leaders preaching unity while practicing division, claiming to fight for the people while building mansions in Damansara Heights, demanding loyalty while demonstrating none themselves.

What this split really exposes is the fundamental bankruptcy of politics built purely on identity and grievance rather than governance and solutions. For the ordinary supporters who have invested decades of faith, energy, and resources into this movement, the cognitive dissonance must be overwhelming. The most likely outcome, as the video explores, is not a dramatic awakening but a slow, grinding demoralization as the gap between the promise and the reality becomes impossible to ignore. Meanwhile, the merry-go-round continues: blame will be deflected, scapegoats will be found, and the cycle will repeat until enough people decide to focus on actually improving their own lives rather than waiting for political saviors who are too busy fighting each other to deliver on any promises.

Text:
Presiden Bersatu, Muhyiddin Yassin mengesahkan peletakan jawatan sebagai Pengerusi Perikatan Nasional, PN, berkuat kuasa 1 Januari ini.

Perkara itu dimaklumkan melalui satu kenyataan rasmi ringkas, tanpa menyatakan sebab peletakan jawatan tersebut.

Ahli Parlimen Pagoh itu turut merakamkan penghargaan kepada seluruh kepimpinan PN yang menyokongnya sepanjang lima tahun menerajui gabungan berkenaan.

Lead counsel for former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, Datuk Hisyam Teh Pok Teik, said the criminal charges against his client are vague, placing the defence at a disadvantage in preparing its case.

Speaking after trial proceedings at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Monday (March 9), he said the charge documents lack clear details on how the alleged offences were committed or what actions were purportedly taken by Muhyiddin.

Meanwhile, lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad said the prosecution had yet to establish the relevance of TikTok videos presented in court by a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer.

PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang said the PAS central working committee made the decision in a special meeting held last night.
